tagline.text: The island where the world's sweetest mangoes ripen

children.text: The home of the Philippines' most celebrated mangoes, just a
15-minute
bangka ride from Iloilo. With mango farms and mango pizza, a Trappist monastery, and island hopping around small islets on the south coast, you can leisurely explore the whole island in a day or two.

Guimaras is an island of about 600 km² floating in the Guimaras Strait between Panay and Negros, and a small province where the whole island forms a single provincial unit. Long part of Iloilo province, it became a separate province in
and is made up of five municipalities: Jordan (the capital), Buenavista, Nueva Valencia, San Lorenzo, and Sibunag. It's only
15 minutes
by sea from Parola wharf in Iloilo City, yet the moment you set foot on the island, city noise gives way to a quiet countryside dotted with mango trees.

What put Guimaras on the map nationwide is its mangoes. Among the Philippines' carabao mangoes, those grown in Guimaras are famous for their high sweetness and rich aroma, and the island is home to the National Mango Research and Development Center. Mangoes are prized here to the point that bringing outside mangoes onto the island is banned, in order to protect the island's mango quality and keep it free of pests and disease. Every
May
, the Manggahan Festival celebrates the mango harvest.

The southwestern coast of the island, around Nueva Valencia, has its own charm. Around Alubihod Beach, small uninhabited islets and limestone rock formations are scattered offshore, and the Taklong Island National Marine Reserve is a well-preserved ecological area of mangroves and coral reefs. Attractions are scattered across the island, including Guisi Beach with its Spanish-era lighthouse ruins, the hilltop pilgrimage site of Balaan Bukid, and the Trappist monastery where monks make mango jam.

Guimaras suits travellers who'd rather enjoy a quiet island village, fresh fruit, and simple beaches than big resorts or flashy activities. It's a nice day trip from Iloilo, and equally good for an unhurried overnight stay at a beach resort.

blocks.title: Eat mangoes and visit a mango farm

children.text: In season (roughly March to
May
), you can buy freshly picked mangoes cheaply from roadside stalls and markets. Walk among the mango trees around a farm or near the research center.
Mango pizza, sold at restaurants around Jordan, is a local specialty — a sweet-and-savory pie topped with cashews and mango, best enjoyed with a mango shake.

Our Lady of the Philippines Trappist Monastery, in San Miguel, Jordan, has a peaceful grounds and a simple chapel that leave an impression. The monastery gift shop sells mango jam, mango cookies, and cashew products.
Rent a bangka at Alubihod Beach in Nueva Valencia to visit Ave Maria Island, small caves and rock islets, and snorkeling spots. A boat costs around

A protected area combining mangrove forest, seagrass beds, and coral reefs, known for its striking scenery of limestone rock islands cloaked in green forest. Entry and activities follow the reserve's management rules.

children.text: The ruins of a stone lighthouse built in the
during the Spanish era stand on a hill above the beach. A newer lighthouse stands beside it, and the beach below is a quiet spot for swimming.

A hilltop shrine in Jordan topped with a giant cross; climb the steps for a view over the Guimaras Strait and Iloilo City. On Good Friday, the passion play "Ang Pagtaltal sa Guimaras" is performed here.
An early-20th-century mansion built on a rock outcrop on the Buenavista coast, once the summer home of a prominent Iloilo family. Enjoy the exterior along with the coastal view.

from Manila to Iloilo International Airport (ILO). From the airport to Parola wharf downtown takes about
45 minutes–1 hour

Motorized bangkas run from Parola wharf in Iloilo City to Jordan wharf roughly every
15 minutes
(every
30 minutes–1 hour
during quiet periods), costing about
per person. The first boat runs before dawn, and the last is usually around
6–7 PM
There is also a route toward Buenavista, and if you want to bring a vehicle across, take a RoRo ferry to Jordan from Iloilo's RoRo terminal.
Bangka fares and schedules can change based on decisions by shipping authorities and the provincial government, so check the latest notice.
Coming from Bacolod, take a fast craft to Iloilo first (about
1 hour
), then head to Parola wharf.

On the island, tricycles or multicabs (small truck-based jeepneys) are the way to get around. You can charter a fixed-rate tricycle for an island loop at the tourist information center by Jordan wharf, costing about
a day depending on the route.
A shared jeepney or multicab from Jordan to Nueva Valencia costs about
per person and takes about

The dry season, from
December
to
May
, is best for touring the island and enjoying the beaches. In particular, from
March
to
May
is the peak of the mango harvest, when you can eat the best mangoes at the lowest prices. Around the provincial founding anniversary in
late May
, the Manggahan Festival brings a mango-eating contest, a parade, and an agricultural fair.
From
June
to
November
is the rainy season, and afternoon showers and the southwest monsoon can lead to cancelled hopping tours in the southern waters some days. Typhoons mainly affect the area between August and
November
, and bangka service between Iloilo and Guimaras can be suspended during these. Visitor numbers rise sharply during Holy Week before Easter, for the Balaan Bukid pilgrimage and passion play.

Guimaras accommodation is concentrated mostly around Alubihod Beach in Nueva Valencia. Beachfront bungalows and small to mid-size resorts run about

a night, and weekends in peak season get crowded with day-trippers and overnight visitors from Iloilo, so book ahead. There are also small hotels and guesthouses near Jordan, the provincial capital, which you can choose based on how you plan your island loop.

Mangoes are, without question, the star of the food here. You can try nearly every dish made with mango — fresh mango, mango shakes, mango pizza, mango ketchup, mango jam, and dried mango. Beach resorts and coastal restaurants serve grilled fish, squid, and shellfish dishes at reasonable prices. Mango jam and cookies from the Trappist monastery gift shop, and dried mango from the souvenir shops in front of Jordan wharf, make popular gifts.
When you arrive at Jordan wharf, check the island map and the fixed tricycle rates at the tourist information center first — it leads to fewer disputes than negotiating individually with touts.
The island loop covers quite a distance. If you're only visiting for the day, it's best to focus on either the north (monastery, pilgrimage site, mangoes) or the south (beaches, hopping).
ATMs are only found in a few places, such as Jordan, so bring enough cash from Iloilo.
Mangoes cost much more and taste less good outside the harvest season. A visit from March to
May
is recommended.
Taking mango souvenirs back to Iloilo is fine, but check quarantine rules for air travel and for taking them abroad. Bringing fresh mangoes into Korea is generally not allowed.

Alubihod Beach gets shallow at low tide. Plan your swimming and hopping around the tide schedule.
Bringing mangoes or mango saplings bought outside Guimaras onto the island is prohibited. They will be confiscated if found during quarantine checks at the wharf.
Collecting coral or shells, fishing, and touching marine life are banned in the marine reserve. Follow the guidance of the reserve staff.
Bangka service is suspended when waves run high. During the rainy season, build extra time into your schedule and always wear a life jacket.
Rural roads have very little lighting at night. Avoid renting a motorbike for nighttime driving.
Entrance fees and environmental charges at well-known attractions vary by municipality and change from time to time, so check the latest notice.
